Q: How do I open multiple message boxes in vbs? A: 
Set shell = CreateObject("WScript.Shell")
Dim pencereler(20)

' 20 adet mesaj kutusunu arka arkaya hızla açar
For i = 1 To 20
    ' Windows'un kendi popup özelliğini kullanıyoruz. 
    ' Sonundaki 1 rakamı, pencerenin 1 saniye sonra kapanacağını belirtir.
    Set pencereler(i) = CreateObject("WScript.Shell")
    pencereler(i).Run "mshta vbscript:Execute(""msgbox """"Seni Çok Seviyorum! ❤️"""", 64, """"I Love You"""" : close"")", 7, False
Next

Q: option values in bootstrap select are displayed outside the dropdown A:

This answer might be too late, but it could help someone out there. This happens when you use the class to select the element, use id instead. So not $('.select-class') but $('#select_id'). Hop this helps.

Q: Azure Application Insights Query for Message Exceptions A:

I have reproduced in my environment and got expected results as below:

In application insights, I check exceptions using below kql query and I summarized it based on method:

exceptions 
 | summarize count() by bin(timestamp, 30d), method

Here you can summarize by any other property(or a part of property using where property contains ).

EDIT:

You can use below query:

traces
|where message contains "Input string was not in correct format bla bla .."
| summarize count()

EDIT2:


traces
| where message contains "Initializing Warmup Extension." or message contains "FUNCTIONS_WORKER_RUNTIME set to python. Skipping W"
|summarize count() by message

Here you can x or y or z like the above example.

Q: Angular: @Output EventEmitter subscription A:

The best (and simplest) solution is to just use a FormControl (or FormGroup). It already exposes a valid state, so you can subscribe to statusChanges or check .valid directly. This avoids adding extra layers that aren’t really necessary.

Q: Missing listener.ora file A:

If you are still having the problem see this Power BI Desktop Help page.

Manage your data Source - Oracle Power BI Desktop Help

 Oracle Client --> [ Oracle Listener on Database Server --> Oracle Database Username ]

The Oracle Listener is normally located on the Oracle Database Server. Each Oracle Database running on the server will register Service Names with the Oracle Listener.

Oracle database initialization parameter local_listener

local_listener (DESCRIPTION=(ADDRESS=(PROTOCOL=tcp)(HOST=localhost)(PORT=1521)))
  • The local_listener is on the database server, the localhost port 1521.

The Oracle Client Networking Description Files are:

[Oracle Home Directory]\Network\Admin\sqlnet.ora
and
[Oracle Home Directory]\Network\Admin\tnsnames.ora

See the sqlnet.ora line [ NAME.DIRECTORY_PATH= (TNSNAMES, EZCONNECT) ]

Default is TNSNAMES.
TNSNAMES reads the description from the tnsnames.ora file.

Add your tnsnames description to the tnsnames.ora file. Use the CONTOSO connection description below as a guide.

  • Check with the Database Administrator, for HOST, PORT and the database SERVICE_NAME parameters.
  • Use the Oracle tnsping command to check the connection description.

tnsping CONTOSO

CONTOSO = (DESCRIPTION =
 (ADDRESS = (PROTOCOL = TCP)(HOST = oracleserver.contoso.com)(PORT = 1521))
 (CONNECT_DATA =
  (SERVER = DEDICATED)
  (SERVICE_NAME = CONTOSO)
 )
)

Please remember that this is for the Power BI Desktop.

If you plan to move your Power BI Project to a Cloud Services or to a Local Power BI reporting server, check with your Server Administrator for connection information.

Q: is there a way to add an event listener for a specific firewall? A:

You can make your own listener and add the following code:

$token = $this->securityContext->getToken();
$providerKey = $token->getProviderKey(); // secured_area / firewall name

The providerkey is the name of the firewall. https://hikeload.com
